title: Coronation Chicken Sandwich
subtitle: Cold coronation chicken filling in soft white or brown bread
excerpt: Coronation chicken filling, the mild curry-spiced mayonnaise with mango chutney and sultanas, generously loaded into soft bread. The most popular non-plain sandwich filling in British deli and sandwich shops.
sourceNotes: Based on coronation chicken, developed for the coronation banquet of Queen Elizabeth II in 1953 by Constance Spry and Rosemary Hume. The sandwich version became standard in British deli counters and sandwich shops from the 1980s onwards. Recipe developed from first principles.

recipe.batchNotes: Make the filling in bulk and keep in the fridge. Assemble sandwiches as needed.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days. Assemble sandwiches up to 2 hours before serving.

content.text: Coronation chicken sandwich is the filling from coronation chicken, a mildly spiced mayonnaise sauce with mango chutney and sultanas, loaded generously into soft bread with optional lettuce. The filling is better after 30 minutes in the fridge so the flavours settle. Make the chicken first, then assemble the sandwiches.

Mix {{mayonnaise}} of mayonnaise with {{curry-powder}} of mild curry powder, {{mango-chutney}} of mango chutney, the juice of {{lemon}}, and {{sultanas}} of sultanas if using. Taste and adjust: more curry powder if bland, more lemon juice if too sweet.
Add {{chicken-breast}} of shredded cooked chicken and fold gently to coat. Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Butter {{bread-white}} bread slices with {{salted-butter}} if using. Pile the filling generously onto 4 slices. Close with the remaining slices, press lightly, and cut in half.

rows.cause: Chutney too generous or curry powder too mild
rows.fix: Add more lemon juice and an extra pinch of curry powder. Taste and adjust before adding the chicken.

rows.cause: Filling too loose or sandwich assembled too early
rows.fix: The filling should be thick enough to heap without spreading. Assemble within 2 hours of serving.

rows.cause: Breast meat overcooked or not enough sauce
rows.fix: Make sure there is enough mayonnaise to coat all the chicken generously. Thigh meat is also a good option for juicier results.

rows.cause: Powdered spice added cold to the sauce without toasting
rows.fix: Toast the curry powder in a dry pan for 30 seconds before mixing in. It rounds off the raw spice note.

content.text: Coronation chicken became a sandwich filling in British deli culture during the 1980s, as the pre-made sandwich market grew. By the 1990s it was among the top-selling pre-packaged sandwich fillings in the country, sold in supermarkets, petrol stations, and lunch shops. The sandwich format made the 1953 coronation banquet dish part of everyday British food in a way that serving it on a plate never quite achieved.
